title: Cell-Free Protein Synthesis from Exonuclease-Deficient Cellular Extracts Utilizing Linear DNA Templates
protocol: Weigh 0.34 g of chloramphenicol and add ethanol to 10 mL.
Mix the chloramphenicol solution until dissolved.
Aliquot 1 mL each into several tubes and store at -20°C.
Prepare S30A buffer according to Table 2, aiming for 2 L.
Adjust pH to 7.7 using glacial acetic acid before autoclaving.
Autoclave the S30A buffer.
Keep the S30A buffer at 4°C after autoclaving.
Add DTT filtered by a 0.22 μm membrane filter to reach a final concentration of 2 mM in S30A buffer.
Prepare stock solutions according to Table 3 and keep them on ice.
Calibrate the pH as requested for the indicated components using Tris buffer or KOH, as specified in Table 3.
Add each component volume into a 15 mL tube in the order indicated in Table 3.
Aliquot energy solution at 150 μL per tube.
Flash freeze aliquots on dry ice and store at -80°C.
Thaw amino acid tubes by vortexing and incubate at 37°C until completely dissolved.
Add 12 ml of sterile water to a 50 mL tube.
Add 1.5 ml each of the amino acids in the order indicated in Table 4.
Vortex until the solution is fairly clear.
Incubate at 37°C if necessary.
Aliquot 500 μL of the amino acid solution per tube on ice.
Flash-freeze the aliquots on dry ice.
Store the aliquots at -80°C.
Prepare a stock solution for Mg-glu (100 mM).
Prepare a stock solution for K-glu (3 M).
Make a serial dilution from these stocks for Mg-glu (0 to 20 mM).
Make a serial dilution from these stocks for K-glu (20 to 300 mM).
Prepare 50 mL of 40% PEG8000 solution.
Streak strain BL21 Rosetta2 ΔrecBCD from -80°C glycerol stock onto a 2xYT+P agar plate with 10 μg/mL chloramphenicol.
Incubate overnight at 37°C.
Inoculate a single colony into 10 mL of 2xYT+P supplemented with 10 μg/mL chloramphenicol.
Incubate overnight at 37°C with 200 rpm shaking.
Make a subculture by diluting the overnight culture 100 times into 4 L of fresh 2xYT+P media containing 10 µg/mL chloramphenicol.
Incubate at 37 °C, 200 rpm for about 3 to 4 h of growth until an OD600 of 1.5-2.0 is reached.
Dilute the culture by 4x if measuring OD600 > 0.8.
Put the culture on ice.
Spin down the cells at 5,000 x g for 12 min at 4 °C.
Discard the supernatant by decanting.
Resuspend the cell pellets in 800 mL of chilled S30A+DTT.
Repeat steps 2.3.5 and 2.3.6.
Spin down the cells at 5,000 x g for 12 min at 4 °C.
Discard the supernatant by decanting.
Resuspend cell pellets in 160 mL of chilled S30A+DTT.
Resuspend cell pellets in S30A+DTT buffer at a ratio of 25 times less than the original cell culture volume.
Transfer cells to chilled and pre-weighed 50 mL tubes.
Spin down the cells at 2,000 x g for 8 min at 4 °C.
Discard supernatant by decanting.
Spin down the cells again at 2,000 x g for 4 min at 4 °C.
Remove remaining supernatant carefully with a pipette.
Re-measure weight of the tube to calculate weight of the cell pellet.
Keep the cell pellets at -80°C.
Thaw cell pellets on ice for 1-2 hours.
Resuspend cell pellets in S30A+DTT buffer at 0.9 mL per gram of pellets' weight.
Pipette slowly to resuspend cells, avoiding top froth as much as possible.
Place 1 mL aliquots of the resuspended cells into 1.5 mL microtubes.
Keep tubes on ice or in a pre-chilled cold block at 4°C.
Sonicate each tube in a sonicator with a 3 mm probe and frequency of 20 kHz.
Set up the sonication with an amplitude of 20%.
Perform three cycles of sonication (30 s sonication, 1 min pause).
Keep the tubes on a cold block surrounded by ice during sonication.
Alternate between two pre-chilled cold blocks to prevent overheating.
Spin down the lysate at 12,000 x g for 10 min at 4 °C.
Collect the supernatant with a pipette and transfer it to a 50 mL tube.
Incubate the cell lysate at 37 °C with agitation at 200 rpm for 80 min.
Spin down the lysate again at 12,000 x g for 10 min at 4 °C.
Collect the supernatant and aliquot 30 µL each into pre-chilled 1.5 mL microtubes.
Keep all tubes on ice during the aliquoting process.
Flash-freeze the lysate aliquots on dry ice.
Store the flash-frozen lysate aliquots at -80 °C.
Calibrate cell-free buffer for optimal Mg-glu and K-glu concentrations as described in Sun et al.
Prepare reactions to a final volume of 10.5 μL each.
Thaw all components on ice before mixing.
Mix 33% of the total reaction volume with cell extract.
Add reporter DNA to a final concentration of 1 nM (linear or plasmid DNA).
Combine cell-free buffer components (PEG8000, AA solution, and energy solution) in the reaction mixture.
Include K-glu at a final concentration of 80 mM.
For each reaction, take different concentrations of Mg-glu from 10x concentrated stocks ranging from 0 to 20 mM.
Add 9.45 μL of Master Mix for each reaction (90% total volume).
Gently mix the reactions.
Use PCR eight-strip tubes to prepare dilutions.
Mix with a multichannel pipette.
Pipette 10 µL of the reactions into a 384-well square-bottom microplate.
Cover the plate using an adhesive plate seal.
Measure gene expression as fluorescence output.
Record fluorescence data with a plate reader (Ex: 485 nm; Em: 528 nm) at regular intervals for 8 h of incubation at 30 °C with continuous orbital shaking at 307 cpm.
Spin down the 384-well microplate (<2,500 x g, 1 min, room temperature) before starting data acquisition if needed.
Identify the Mg-glu concentration that results in the highest fluorescence value at the end-point.
Repeat step with more diverse concentration ranges if unsure about the optimal Mg-glu concentration obtained.
Proceed to K-glu calibration for a range of concentrations (20, 40, 60, 80, 100, 120, 140, 160, 180, 200, 220, and 240 mM) using the same volumes indicated in step.
Run the experiment to identify the highest fluorescence value from among the K-glu concentrations tested.
PCR amplify from plasmid P70a-deGFP using DNA polymerase with oligo primers listed in Table 7.
Set up the PCR reactions in a 50 µL volume according to the manufacturer's protocol.
Incubate at 98 °C for 2 min, followed by 40 cycles of 98 °C for 30 s, 66 °C for 30 s, and 72 °C for 60 s; then incubate at 72 °C for 10 min and 4 °C indefinitely.
Add 1 µL of DpnI restriction enzyme per 50 µL PCR reaction and incubate at 37 °C for 1 h.
Purify the PCR reaction using a PCR & DNA cleanup Kit and elute in nuclease-free water.
Verify the PCR products on a 1% agarose gel (1x TAE) prior to use.
Quantify purified PCR products or plasmid preps using Nanodrop (ND-1,000).
Measure concentration of unpurified DNA using a fluorometric assay with DNA-binding dye if compatible with downstream cell-free reaction.
Calibrate buffer stock for each lysate batch prepared using Supplementary File 1.
Use the ‘Reaction Preparation’ tab in Supplementary File 1 to set up subsequent cell-free reactions.
Pipette 5 nM of each template into the reaction mixture for cell-free expression.
Set the volume of each reaction at 10.5 µL, pipetting only 10 µL into a 384-well plate for data acquisition.
Use consistent pipettes and tip types when dispensing reactions to avoid bubbles or liquid sticking to well walls.
Spin down the plate if needed (<2,500 x g, 1 min, room temperature) to ensure uniform distribution of the reaction mixture.
Label a 1.5 mL microtube for the Optimal Master Mix preparation (separately for linear and plasmid DNA).
Add the correct volumes of Buffer and Lysate, and mix gently.
Pipette DNA samples first, followed by nuclease-free water, and finally the Optimal Master Mix from step 5.2.
Mix the cell-free reaction gently with a pipette just before adding to the plate reader.
Set up the reactions in the plate reader (Ex 485 nm; Em 528 nm).
Record fluorescence data at regular intervals for 8 h of incubation at 30 °C, with continuous orbital shaking.
Store NIST-FITC stock solution at 4°C.
Store recombinant eGFP at -20°C.
Prepare a solution of 100 mM sodium borate, pH 9.5.
Store the sodium borate solution at room temperature or at 4°C.
Prepare 12 dilutions (70 μL each) of NIST-traceable FITC standard using sodium borate solution in triplicate.
Dilute the FITC stock from 50 µM to concentrations of 50, 25, 12.5, 6.25, 3.125, 1.562, 0.781, 0.390, 0.195, 0.097, and 0 µM.
Prepare serial dilutions (70 μL each) of recombinant eGFP using sodium borate solution in triplicate.
Dilute the eGFP stock to concentrations of 1.2, 0.3, 0.075, 0.0188, 0.0047, 0.0012, 0.0003, 0.00007, and 0 µM.
Add 20 μL of each dilution (nine wells each) into a 384-well square-bottom microplate.
Cover the microplate with an adhesive plate seal.
Incubate the microplate in a plate reader for measurement.
Acquire GFP fluorescence data using Excitation: 485/20, Emission: 528/20, and gain 50 settings.
Save data for FITC and eGFP calibration.
Calculate relative measurements using the example in Table 9.
Divide values obtained in fluorescence arbitrary units (a.u.) by the curve slope "a" value (y = ax).
Estimate GFP production in terms of FITC or eGFP.
